o1.biggest_strength: It understands the real launch risk: migration. The go/no-go gates, staged rollout, support prep, creator focus, and author credit are all very usable.
o1.biggest_mistake: The channel ranking is a little confused: the table shows retained-user math, but the rank order does not fully match either retained users or retention rate. I would want that tightened before using it.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the channel ranking explicit and defensible, add owners to the timeline, reduce a few absolute claims like “Nothing to set up again,” and turn placeholders into final measured claims or remove them.

o2.biggest_strength: It puts the right bets first: creators, extension authors, migration safety, support readiness, and a staged update. It also feels practical for the small team and the code-freeze date.
o2.biggest_mistake: The channel table is labeled as ranked by users kept, but the order favors quality and scalability over the literal retained-user totals. That needs one sentence of explanation to avoid looking mathematically inconsistent.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Clarify the ranking logic, make the X post a short thread with separate clips and author credits, and soften “Extension authors tested this version” unless we know enough authors actually did.

reason: I would rather run Output 2. It is sharper, more operational, and more faithful to how Raycast should launch: community first, migration risk controlled, and no wasted energy chasing low-retention noise.
